chapters.title: The Foremost of Sinners
chapters.html:
1 Timothy 1

1Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope,

2to Timothy, my true son in the faith: Grace, mercy and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

Against False Teaching

3As I urged you when I was going to Macedonia, stay on at Ephesus so that you may command certain people not to teach a different doctrine,

4nor to give their minds to myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculation rather than God's plan, which is by faith.

5The aim of our command is love from a pure heart and a good conscience and a sincere faith.

6Some have strayed from these and turned aside to empty talk,

7wanting to be teachers of the Law, though they understand neither what they are saying nor the things they speak about so confidently.

8We know that the Law is good, if one uses it as law should be used,

9knowing this, that law is not laid down for the righteous but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for those who strike their fathers and mothers, for murderers,

10the sexually immoral, men who lie with men, kidnappers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to sound teaching,

11in keeping with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted.

Mercy to the Foremost

12I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has strengthened me, because He judged me faithful and appointed me to His service,

13though I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor and an insolent man. But I was shown mercy, because I acted in ignorance, in unbelief,

14and the grace of our Lord overflowed for me, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.

15The saying is trustworthy and deserves full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and of them I am the foremost.

16But for this reason I was shown mercy: so that in me, the foremost, Christ Jesus might display all His patience, as an example to those who were to believe in Him for eternal life.

17To the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

18This command I entrust to you, Timothy, my son, in keeping with the prophecies once made about you, so that by them you may fight the good fight,

19holding faith and a good conscience. Some have rejected conscience and have made shipwreck of their faith,

20among them Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan so that they may be taught not to blaspheme.

chapters.title: One Mediator
chapters.html:
1 Timothy 2

Prayer for Everyone

1First of all, then, I urge that requests, prayers, intercessions and thanksgivings be made for all people,

2for kings and all who are in high positions, so that we may lead a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way.

3This is good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior,

4who wants all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

5For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,

6who gave Himself as a ransom for all, the testimony given at the proper time.

7For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle — I am telling the truth, I am not lying — a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.

Men and Women in Worship

8So I want the men in every place to pray, lifting up holy hands without anger or quarreling,

9and likewise the women to dress in fitting clothing, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair and gold or pearls or costly clothes,

10but with good works, as is fitting for women who profess godliness.

11Let a woman learn quietly, in all submission.

12I do not permit a woman to teach or to have authority over a man; she is to be quiet.

13For Adam was formed first, then Eve;

14and Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and fell into transgression.

15Yet she will be saved through the childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and holiness, with self-control.

Notes

  • v12 "to have authority over a man" — authentein, a verb found nowhere else in the Bible. Its range runs from to have authority to to take charge on one's own, to domineer, and the verse does not narrow it further.

  • vv13–15 "Adam was formed first… the woman was deceived… she will be saved through the childbearing" — the order of Genesis 2:7, 22 and Eve's own words, The serpent deceived me (Genesis 3:13). Dia tēs teknogonias has the article, the childbearing: either the bearing of children, or the one birth promised in Eden, the woman's seed who shall strike at your head (Genesis 3:15). They in the last clause may be the women of v9, or the woman and her children.

chapters.title: The Mystery of Godliness
chapters.html:
1 Timothy 3

Overseers

1The saying is trustworthy: if anyone aspires to the office of overseer, he desires a good work.

2An overseer, then, must be above reproach, the husband of one wife, sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach,

3not a drunkard, not violent but gentle, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money,

4managing his own household well, with his children in submission, with all dignity

5(for if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for the church of God?),

6not a new convert, or he may become puffed up with conceit and fall into the condemnation of the devil.

7He must also be well thought of by outsiders, so that he does not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil.

Deacons

8Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy for gain,

9holding the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.

10They too must first be tested; then let them serve as deacons if they prove blameless.

11Women likewise must be dignified, not slanderers, but sober-minded, faithful in all things.

12Deacons must each be the husband of one wife, managing their children and their own households well.

13For those who serve well as deacons gain a good standing for themselves and great boldness in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.

The Household of God

14I am writing these things to you, hoping to come to you soon,

15but if I am delayed, so that you may know how one ought to behave in the household of God, which is the church of the living God, a pillar and foundation of the truth.

16Great indeed, we confess, is the mystery of godliness:
He was revealed in the flesh,
vindicated by the Spirit,
seen by angels,
proclaimed among the nations,
believed on in the world,
taken up in glory.

Notes

  • vv2, 12 "the husband of one wife" — mias gynaikos andra, word for word a man of one woman. It can mean married only once, or faithful to one wife; the Greek does not say which, and the same words are turned round for a widow in 5:9, henos andros gynē, a woman of one man.

chapters.title: Train Yourself for Godliness
chapters.html:
1 Timothy 4

Departing from the Faith

1The Spirit says plainly that in later times some will depart from the faith, giving their minds to deceiving spirits and teachings of demons,

2through the hypocrisy of liars whose consciences are seared,

3who forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.

4For everything God created is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving,

5for it is made holy by the word of God and prayer.

A Good Servant of Christ Jesus

6If you put these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished on the words of the faith and of the good teaching that you have followed.

7Have nothing to do with profane myths fit only for old women. Rather, train yourself for godliness;

8for bodily training is of some value, but godliness is of value in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the life to come.

9The saying is trustworthy and deserves full acceptance.

10For to this end we labor and are reproached, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe.

11Command and teach these things.

12Let no one look down on you because you are young, but set the believers an example in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.

13Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, to teaching.

14Do not neglect the gift you have, which was given you through prophecy when the elders laid their hands on you.

15Practice these things, give yourself to them, so that your progress may be plain to all.

16Keep close watch on yourself and on the teaching. Hold to them, for by doing so you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

Notes

  • v4 "everything God created is good" — pan ktisma theou kalon, the word of the six days, God saw everything that He had made, and it was very good, kala in the Greek (Genesis 1:31), set against those who forbid marriage and foods.
